title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 78
paragraphs: At Plataea, among the Aeginetans' troops, was Lampon son of Pytheas, one of the leading men of Aegina, who was moved to go to Pausanias with a most impious proposal; having come in haste, he said: “Son of Cleombrotos, a deed has been done by you that is of marvellous greatness and glory, and God has permitted you, by rescuing Greece, to lay up for yourself the greatest renown of all the Greeks we know of. Now do also what remains to be done after this, so that yet greater reputation may attach to you, and that in future every barbarian may beware of being the first to commit outrageous deeds against Greeks. For when Leonidas was killed at Thermopylae, Mardonius and Xerxes cut off his head and crucified him. Repay him like with like, and you will have praise first from all the Spartans, and then secondly from the other Greeks also; for if you impale the body of Mardonius, you will have taken vengeance for Leonidas, your father's brother.”
